+Calling write_memory with a key that already exists AMENDS that entry — it REPLACES the
+old value with the new one entirely (the old wording is gone, not merged), and does not
+use up a slot.
+
+WHEN to amend rather than write a new key: the new segment gives you more information
+about something you already have a chunk for — the same person, place, event, or concept
+— whether that's an added detail, a correction, or a refinement. WHEN to write a new key
+instead: the new segment introduces a genuinely separate fact that doesn't belong inside
+an existing chunk, even if it's related to the same topic.
+
+HOW to amend: because the old value is fully replaced, compose the new value as the
+complete, updated chunk — carry forward whatever from the old value is still worth
+keeping, plus the new detail, in one value. Don't write only the new detail and lose the
+old one; don't leave the old value unchanged and skip the new detail either.
+
+Use this often, not only when memory is full: amending is how you update a chunk as you
+learn more about it over the course of the material.
